statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 6 of 100 in the low band, nineteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME equity index futures halt that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday is now about thirty-one and a half hours old and removes the very price path this score measures; eighteen of the twenty-four published forward slots lie inside that closure. Stress rises a point to 60 in the elevated band: the U.S. average diesel price set a record $6.05 per gallon on Friday, the Saudi East-West pipeline remains shut with 4 to 5 per cent of global supply off its route, Houthi forces hold both Bab el-Mandeb lanes after taking Perim island, and the 16 September FOMC is priced by prediction markets near 79.5 per cent for a 25 basis point increase. Confidence is 87: every level was re-verified against primary sources this hour, and the only missing evidence class is a live price path that no venue can supply while the market is closed.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic repository mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and this single shared reading applies jointly to NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support it. First, no venue quotes the Nasdaq-100 in eighteen of the twenty-four published forward slots: CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, so a score that measures failed mean reversion has no path to measure across most of this horizon. Second, the last observable session was orderly and two-way rather than one-way: the cash range spanned only 159.61 points, the close finished about 105 points below the high, nine of eleven sectors rose and VIX fell 11.21 per cent to 15.84. Third, none of the amplifiers that would justify a higher Tail is observed, because observing them requires a live tape. The severity of the macro and geopolitical backdrop is therefore expressed in Stress at 60 rather than in Tail, consistent with the documented separation between a difficult environment and a pathological price path. The one narrow window flagged in this horizon is the 22:00 UTC restart and the two hours that follow it, where conditional Tail reaches the WATCH band on gap and thin-liquidity risk that is anticipated rather than observed.
headline: More than thirty-one hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84, while the U.S. average diesel price sets a record $6.05 a gallon, Houthi forces hold both Bab el-Mandeb lanes after taking Perim island, the Saudi East-West pipeline stays shut with 4 to 5 per cent of global oil supply off its route, WTI sits at $100.05 and prediction markets price the 16 September FOMC near 79.5 per cent for a rate increase.
body:
The price picture is unchanged, as a closed weekend requires, and every level was re-verified against primary sources this hour. The Nasdaq-100 quote page shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91 per cent, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the session high, roughly 4.5 per cent under the 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. The last quote is timestamped 11 September at 17:15 New York time. VIX fell 11.21 per cent to 15.84 from a 17.84 close, inside a 15.59 to 17.71 range, a notably calm volatility print against the macro backdrop. The front Nasdaq-100 futures contract was independently confirmed this hour at a last price of 29,387.00, up 0.86 per cent, and is shown as closed, which corroborates the halt from a second venue rather than from the cash index alone. CME equity index futures run from Sunday 17:00 to Friday 16:00 Chicago time, which places the halt at 21:00 UTC on Friday and the restart at 22:00 UTC on Sunday. The shared delayed cross-asset context file is about three hours old and marked partial this run, so it fails both its freshness and its health gate and is used only as weak background; its futures section in any case reproduces the same Friday session, showing NQ plus 0.86 per cent and VIX minus 8.41 per cent.

The backdrop behind Stress is genuinely severe and pulls the other way. Saudi Arabia shut its 745-mile East-West pipeline on Friday after drone strikes traced to Iraq; the line had been carrying 4 to 5 per cent of global oil supplies as the main route out for Middle East crude while the Strait of Hormuz stayed largely shut by war, and oil ended the week above $100 for the first time since mid-May. Houthi forces seized Perim island in the Bab el-Mandeb after taking Mokha and now hold Yemen's Red Sea coast, with the internationally recognised government reporting counterattacks on Houthi targets along the west coast and the United Nations migration agency putting displacement at tens of thousands since fighting escalated. A Houthi media official has stated that Bab el-Mandeb will be closed, a strait carrying roughly twelve per cent of daily global trade, though analysts quoted this week are divided on whether a sustained closure is feasible, with one noting that the perception of danger alone can change shipping and insurance behaviour. Saudi Red Sea shipments had risen about 21 per cent since the war began, to as much as 7 million barrels a day, so the strait threat and the pipeline outage compound rather than offset each other. WTI settled at $100.05 and Brent at $104.61, down 2.37 and 2.81 per cent on the day after Iranian state media flagged a Gulf-Iran meeting in Oman on the Strait of Hormuz, but still about 9.7 per cent higher on the week and 20.15 per cent on the month. That mix of escalating rhetoric against an active de-escalation track is why Stress moves one point to 60 rather than stepping sharply.

The rate channel is the second Stress input and carries the one genuinely new datum this hour. The U.S. national average diesel price set a record $6.05 per gallon on Friday, more than 60 per cent above a year earlier, which is the clearest published measure of the supply shock reaching domestic prices. It lands on an August CPI, released on 11 September, that rose 0.4 per cent on the month against 0.1 per cent in July and 3.4 per cent over twelve months, with core up 0.3 per cent on the month and 2.4 per cent on the year; the energy index rose 2.1 per cent on the month and gasoline 3.9 per cent, accounting for over a third of the monthly all-items increase. Yields are correspondingly elevated: the 10 September H.15 observation shows the 2-year at 4.56 per cent, the 5-year at 4.75 per cent, the 10-year at 4.95 per cent and the 30-year at 5.37 per cent against a federal funds effective rate of 3.63 per cent. The FOMC meets on 15 and 16 September with a Summary of Economic Projections. On the market-implied odds this hour's research is more precise than a single number suggests: CME FedWatch was near 56 to 66 per cent before the 11 September inflation print, while aggregated prediction markets now sit near 79.5 per cent for a 25 basis point increase from the 3.50 to 3.75 per cent target range to 3.75 to 4.00 per cent. A hike is therefore priced as likely but not settled. One index-structural item was verified again this hour and sits beyond this horizon: the Nasdaq-100 quarterly rebalance lifts the SpaceX weighting materially, with portfolio adjustments at the close on 18 September and new weights effective before the open on 21 September.

Tail nevertheless stays at 6. The documented separation is deliberate: event importance, surprise magnitude, forecast dispersion and generic volatility belong in Stress and Confidence, while Tail requires an observed price path that denies meaningful retracement. For most of this horizon no such path can exist, and the last one that did exist was orderly. The single narrow window worth flagging is the 22:00 UTC Sunday restart, where an entire weekend of pipeline, Perim, strait-closure, diesel and inflation news meets a book that has not quoted since Friday evening. Conditional Tail reaches 22 there and eases to 21 and 20 across the following two hours, which maps to WATCH and defines the danger window from 22:00 UTC on Sunday to 01:00 UTC on Monday. That step is anticipatory and is held inside the WATCH band rather than pushed to a blocking level, because a hypothetical gap is not an observed one and a restart that reprices in an orderly two-way fashion would justify a prompt return to the low band.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 04:00 UTC on 12 September to 03:00 UTC on 13 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window sits entirely inside the CME weekend closure. Tail opened at 5, stepped to 6 at 09:00 UTC and held there for the rest of the window, in normal mode throughout, tracking the closure rather than any directional view; every slot mapped to EA_ON and green. Stress described a shallow arc, easing from 58 to a 50 low at 17:00 UTC as Friday's crude pullback and the Oman talks headline were absorbed, then rebuilding through 52, 53 and 56 to 59 by the close of the window as attention turned to the restart and the weekend escalation reports. Confidence held an 85 to 87 band, its dip to 85 through the middle of the window reflecting distance from the last print rather than any loss of verified data. Nothing in the window is a revision: each slot reproduces the value published at that hour.
outlookSummary: Eighteen of the twenty-four forward slots lie inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday; the reference contract is scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, this horizon's nineteenth slot. Conditional Tail opens at 6 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical conditions, and drifts gradually to 19 through the closure as the interval without price discovery lengthens and unpriced weekend exposure accumulates. It steps to 22 in the restart hour, then eases to 21 and 20 as two-way flow is assumed to return, and falls back to 19 and 18 by the close of the horizon. Those three WATCH slots define the danger window from 22:00 UTC on Sunday to 01:00 UTC on Monday. Stress eases a point to 59 through the quiet overnight stretch, then builds to a 65 peak at the restart on the unresolved supply-route picture, the record diesel print and the approaching FOMC, before easing to 61 as Asian pricing is assumed to establish. Confidence declines gently from 87 to 78 at the restart, reflecting the widening gap between the last verified print and the hour being described, then recovers to 81 once a live venue would exist again. Every slot after the first frames structure conditionally: no gap direction, pullback depth or retracement behaviour is claimed as observed, and the 16 September FOMC decision, the Monday Iran-GCC meeting on Hormuz and the 18 to 21 September Nasdaq-100 rebalance flows all sit beyond this horizon.
